# esp-uac2-host

USB Audio Class 2.0 host driver for ESP32-S3. ESP-IDF component written in C. MIT license.

## What This Is

A generic UAC2 host driver that runs on ESP32-S3. It enables the ESP32 to stream audio to/from any USB Audio Class 2.0 device (DACs, audio interfaces, miniDSP hardware). The primary use case is playing measurement sweeps through a miniDSP 2x4 HD for automated subwoofer optimization.

The driver is complete and verified end-to-end against a TinyUSB-based simulator running on a second ESP32-S3. 487,000+ audio frames delivered with zero errors. Not yet tested with real hardware.

## Architecture

```
components/uac2_host/           ESP-IDF component (the driver)
  include/uac2_host.h           Public API: device open/close, stream start/stop/read/write, clock, volume
  include/uac2_desc.h           UAC2 descriptor structs (clock source, terminals, feature unit, AS, format type)
  uac2_host.c                   Driver implementation (~1200 lines)
  uac2_desc.c                   Descriptor parser (~400 lines)
  CMakeLists.txt                Component build file (REQUIRES usb, PRIV_REQUIRES esp_ringbuf)

main/                           Test application
  main.c                        5 automated tests: 48kHz, volume/mute, stop/restart, 44.1kHz, long-running
  tone_gen.c/h                  Sine wave generator for test audio

simulators/simple/              Minimal UAC2 device simulator (TinyUSB on ESP32-S3)
simulators/minidsp-2x4hd/      Full miniDSP 2x4 HD simulator (~1400 lines)
                                UAC2 audio (playback, feedback) + HID (20 commands, EEPROM, DSP state, fault injection)

ref/                            Reference code (read-only, not compiled)
  espressif-uac1/               Espressif's UAC1 host driver v1.3.3 (architecture reference)
  usbx-uac2/                    USBX UAC2 descriptor structs (protocol reference)
  cherryusb-uac2/               CherryUSB UAC2 structs (protocol reference)
  minidsp_2x4hd_descriptors.h   Captured descriptor bytes from real miniDSP hardware
```

## Public API (uac2_host.h)

### Types
- `uac2_host_device_handle_t` — opaque device handle (pointer to internal struct)
- `uac2_stream_dir_t` — `UAC2_STREAM_TX` (playback) or `UAC2_STREAM_RX` (capture)
- `uac2_stream_config_t` — `{ sample_rate, bit_resolution, channels }`
- `uac2_host_event_t` — `TX_DONE`, `RX_DONE`, `TRANSFER_ERROR`, `DISCONNECTED`
- `uac2_host_event_cb_t` — callback signature `void(dev, event, arg)`
- `uac2_device_info_t` — parsed descriptor info (AS interfaces, clock sources, terminals)
- `uac2_sample_rate_range_t` — `{ min, max, res }`

### Functions
```c
// Device lifecycle
esp_err_t uac2_host_device_open(client, usb_dev, event_cb, cb_arg, &handle);
esp_err_t uac2_host_device_close(handle);
esp_err_t uac2_host_device_get_info(handle, &info);

// Streaming
esp_err_t uac2_host_stream_start(handle, dir, &config);
esp_err_t uac2_host_stream_stop(handle, dir);
esp_err_t uac2_host_stream_write(handle, data, size, timeout_ms);  // TX: returns ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT if ringbuf full
esp_err_t uac2_host_stream_read(handle, buf, size, &bytes_read, timeout_ms);  // RX
int64_t   uac2_host_stream_get_start_time(handle);  // microsecond timestamp of first frame

// Clock control
esp_err_t uac2_host_get_sample_rate(handle, &rate);
esp_err_t uac2_host_set_sample_rate(handle, rate);
esp_err_t uac2_host_get_sample_rate_range(handle, ranges[], max, &count);
esp_err_t uac2_host_get_clock_validity(handle, &valid);

// Volume/mute (feature unit)
esp_err_t uac2_host_set_volume(handle, channel, volume_db256);
esp_err_t uac2_host_get_volume(handle, channel, &volume_db256);
esp_err_t uac2_host_set_mute(handle, channel, mute);
esp_err_t uac2_host_get_mute(handle, channel, &mute);

// Event callback
esp_err_t uac2_host_device_set_event_cb(handle, cb, arg);
```

### Constants
```c
#define UAC2_NUM_ISOC_URBS          3       // URBs in flight
#define UAC2_NUM_PACKETS_PER_URB    1       // 1 packet per URB (1ms at Full Speed)
#define UAC2_CTRL_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS   5000
#define UAC2_CTRL_XFER_MAX_SIZE     256
#define UAC2_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS 10      // stops URB re-submission
#define UAC2_MAX_SAMPLE_RATE_RANGES 16
```

## Internal Design

### Stream Lifecycle
1. `stream_start`: find matching AS interface from descriptors → `stream_alloc` (URBs, ringbuf) → `usb_host_interface_claim` → `ctrl_request_no_data(SET_INTERFACE, alt)` → `set_sample_rate` → `stream_submit_urbs`
2. Streaming: TX callback reads from ringbuf, applies feedback-based adaptive packet sizing, resubmits URB. RX callback writes to ringbuf, resubmits.
3. `stream_stop`: set state IDLE under spinlock → `ctrl_request_no_data(SET_INTERFACE, 0)` → endpoint halt/flush/clear → `usb_host_interface_release` → wait for `urbs_in_flight` → `stream_free`

### Feedback Handling
Async playback uses a feedback endpoint (EP IN, isochronous). The device reports its desired sample rate in 10.14 (3-byte, Full Speed) or 16.16 (4-byte) fixed-point format. The driver accumulates the fractional part and adjusts packet size (one extra sample when accumulator overflows). This prevents device buffer drift during sustained playback.

### Control Transfers
All control requests go through `ctrl_request()` which serializes access via a mutex + completion semaphore. For requests with no response data (SET_INTERFACE, SET_CUR), use `ctrl_request_no_data()` which auto-releases the mutex. For GET requests, `ctrl_get_cur`/`ctrl_get_range` wrappers copy response data then release.

### Thread Safety
- `uac2_stream_lock` (portMUX spinlock): protects `stream->state` transitions. Callbacks check state under this lock before resubmitting URBs.
- `ctrl_mutex` (FreeRTOS mutex): serializes control transfer access.
- `urbs_in_flight` (atomic_int): tracks in-flight URBs for clean shutdown.
- `consecutive_errors` (atomic_int): counts errors, stops re-submission at threshold.
- `fb_value` (atomic_uint): feedback value written by feedback callback, read by TX submit.

## Hardware Constraints

- ESP32-S3 USB OTG: Full Speed only (12 Mbps). Sufficient for stereo 48kHz/24-bit (288 bytes/ms = 2.3 Mbps = 25% of bus).
- DWC_OTG FIFO: 1024 bytes total. With PERIODIC_OUT bias: PTX=600, RX=128, NPTX=64.
- Cannot do simultaneous TX+RX: audio capture packets (~294 bytes) exceed the 128-byte RX FIFO.
- VBUS: DevKitC-1 does not supply 5V on OTG port. External power required.

## Kconfig

```
CONFIG_USB_HOST_CONTROL_TRANSFER_MAX_SIZE=512   # miniDSP config descriptor is 373 bytes
CONFIG_USB_HOST_HW_BUFFER_BIAS_PERIODICOUT=y    # Bias FIFO for isochronous OUT
```

## miniDSP 2x4 HD Simulator

Full composite USB device simulator at `simulators/minidsp-2x4hd/`. Runs on a second ESP32-S3 via TinyUSB.

### What It Provides
- VID=0x2752, PID=0x0011, bcdDevice=0x06F2 (matches real device)
- UAC2 audio: playback IF1 (alt 1 = 24-bit, alt 2 = 16-bit), feedback endpoint
- HID IF2: 64-byte vendor reports, 20 commands (ReadHardwareId, ReadFlash, ReadFloats, WriteDSP, WriteBiquad, SetVolume, SetMute, SetConfig, SetSource, etc.)
- EEPROM state, DSP parameter storage, fault injection (serial console toggle)
- All SET_INTERFACE transitions, volume/mute, sample rate switching work

### ISR Safety
`tud_audio_rx_done_isr` runs in USB interrupt context. Must use `ESP_DRAM_LOGI` (not `ESP_LOGI`) with a `DRAM_ATTR` tag. ESP_LOGI acquires a mutex which aborts from ISR context.

## Known Issues / Limitations

- Not tested with real hardware yet (only simulator)
- No HID host support in the driver (HID is separate — the simulator implements the device side)
- `UAC2_HOST_EVENT_DISCONNECTED` is declared but never fired (disconnect detected via USB Host Library client events)
- No suspend/resume API — every stop/start cycle reallocates URBs and ringbuf
- ESP-IDF bug #17707: `usb_host_interface_release()` can fail with ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE. Driver has retry logic (5 attempts, 20ms between).

## Related Projects

- `~/code/minidsp-open` — primary consumer. Needs to play measurement sweeps through miniDSP from ESP32. See `docs/TODO-esp32-usb-audio.md`.
- `~/code/open-sub-optimizer` — calls minidsp-open's `POST /play` API.
- Espressif `usb_host_uac` (github.com/espressif/esp-usb) — UAC1 host driver. Architecture reference, forked patterns.
- USBX (github.com/eclipse-threadx/usbx) — UAC2 descriptor struct reference.

## Building

Requires ESP-IDF v5.4 (`~/esp/esp-idf`). Activate with:
```bash
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" && . ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
```

Build host: `idf.py build` (from repo root)
Build simulator: `cd simulators/minidsp-2x4hd && idf.py build`
Flash: `idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodem<SERIAL> flash`

Serial ports: look for VID 0x1A86 (CH340 UART bridge) in `list_serial_ports`. The right-side USB-C on each DevKitC-1 is the UART port. The left-side is USB OTG (used for device-to-device connection).
